parts.instruction: Write TRUE if the statement is correct, FALSE if it is incorrect.

questions.question: Socrates personally wrote extensive philosophical texts that are still read today.
Plato was a student of Socrates.
According to Aristotle, the vegetative soul is unique to humans.
St. Thomas Aquinas agreed with Plato's idea that the soul is a prisoner of the body.
Descartes believed the body is the true self, not the mind.
John Locke believed humans are born with innate ideas.
No two individuals share the exact same DNA.
The XX chromosome combination indicates a male individual.
Genotype refers to the physical, observable expression of a trait.
The Human Genome Project was completed in 2003.
According to Merleau-Ponty, the self is a product of both idealist and realist standpoints.
In Bronfenbrenner's theory, the Mesosystem refers to interconnections among microsystems.
The Philippine society is traditionally perceived to be individualistic.
According to Mead, the actual self is achieved when the 'I' and 'Me' are congruent.
Clifford Geertz believed in a fixed, universal human essence.
Western philosophy generally focuses on collectivistic nature.
Buddhism's Anatta doctrine teaches that there is no permanent, unchanging self.
In Hinduism, the Atman is subject to reincarnation based on Karma.
Lao Tzu believed that the ego helps us see our true self clearly.
Confucius considered himself a creator of new moral traditions, not a transmitter.
In Freud's model, the Id follows the reality principle.
The Superego contains both the conscience and the ego ideal.
Erikson's theory covers personality development only up to adolescence.
In Erikson's Stage 8, individuals who look back with acceptance experience integrity.
Maslow's Growth Needs arise from lack, not from desire to grow.
Carl Rogers believed every person is born with an actualizing tendency toward growth.
Incongruence in Rogers' theory refers to a perfect match between the real and ideal self.
The Halo Effect can influence grades given to students by teachers.
According to Sternberg, love consists of two components: passion and commitment.
Gender and biological sex refer to the same thing.
